title: The phone
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: The phone rings once at 11 PM. The strip is about the ring.

panels.composition: Wood's bedroom, night. The hallway phone visible through the open door on its little table. WOOD drawing. BARNABY asleep.

image.prompt: a young man drawing at night in his bedroom, a landline phone visible on a small table through the open door in the hallway, a dog asleep, black and white

panels.composition: The phone rings. Once. Drawn big.

image.prompt: a landline phone in a dark hallway ringing, the ring drawn as large jagged sound lines, a young man frozen mid-stroke in the next room

panels.composition: Wood halfway to the door. The phone silent. It rang once.

characters.pose: halfway up from the chair, stopped

image.prompt: a young man half-risen from his chair, stopped, looking at a silent phone in the hallway

panels.composition: Wood back at the table. Not drawing. Barnaby's chin on his slipper. The phone in the door, small, dark.

image.prompt: a young man sitting at his drawing table not drawing, a dog's chin on his slipper, a dark phone visible through the doorway, black and white
image.notes: One ring. Nobody knows who. The strip doesn't decide.

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: One ring at 11 PM. Reserved forever.
